Team —

Following up on the 1:1 last week and the Q1/Q2 calibration notes, I want to start the formal performance support process for Daniel Park (ENG, Platform). Attached is an initial draft PIP (PIP_Draft_DanielPark_v1.docx) that captures the documented gaps and proposed success criteria. High-level summary in case it’s helpful: 

- Primary concerns: repeated missed deliverables on infra tasks, limited cross-team communication, escalation turnaround times > 72 hours.
- Examples: infra-1249 (missed SLA), code review delays (CR-334, CR-341), weekly on-call handoff issues (notes in Ops thread).
- Proposed duration: 60 days (with check-ins every 10 business days).
- Proposed outcomes: measurable reduction in overdue JIRA tickets, consistent participation in on-call rotations, improved code review response time (target <24h).

As this will be a sensitive HR action, I need guidance from People Ops on tone, accommodation language, and required documentation steps, and Legal on wording for the final document. Specific asks: 

1) Laura — can you run the PIP against the People Ops checklist and confirm required next steps (service mailbox, storage location, manager/HR presence for the 1:1)? 
2) Hannah — can you do a light legal review for any language that could be construed as disciplinary rather than supportive?
3) Both — confirm whether 60 or 90 days is recommended given the nature of the role (individual contributor, infra).

I have included links to the performance artifacts in Drive and ticket IDs above. I’d prefer to keep this thread internal until we have final wording; I won’t loop Daniel until HR signs off.

Thanks —
Rishi

Thanks for the clear summary, Rishi. I reviewed the draft and ran it against our PO_Checklist_PIP.pdf. A few quick notes: 

- Success criteria should include objective ticket-based metrics (e.g., reduce overdue infra tickets by 50% and maintain <1 critical miss).
- Add an accommodations paragraph (standard language) and a line about reasonable adjustment requests — HR must receive any accommodation requests in writing.
- Documentation: please attach all 1:1 notes, prior performance review, and on-call logs to HR-4872 in the Drive folder.
- Meeting logistics: HR (me) should attend the initial 1:1 where the plan is formally presented. Please do not send the draft to Daniel before HR attends.

For timeline: 60 days is typically sufficient for clear, measurable infra gaps; for cross-functional behavioral issues we sometimes recommend 90 days. Given the examples you listed, I’d lean 60 days with the option to extend if there’s clear partial progress.

I’ve attached the People Ops checklist for your reference. I’ll book a 30-minute calibration call for Monday, 2026-06-01 09:30 PT with Hannah and you; if that doesn’t work, suggest alternative slots.
